title: Career roadmap · Professor
summary: Build an academic career at the intersection of artificial intelligence, ethics, governance and society through rigorous interdisciplinary research, publications, teaching, grants and policy engagement.

facts.Timeline assumption: The roadmap assumes a 2026-start Ph.D. pathway. Early years develop AI literacy, social-science methods, ethics and governance expertise; later years focus on independent scholarship, grants, teaching, doctoral supervision and institutional leadership.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Establish expertise in AI systems, ethics, responsible AI, social impacts, research methods and technology governance.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Build an independent research niche such as AI governance, algorithmic fairness, AI safety, human-AI interaction or technology policy.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead a multidisciplinary research group, supervise doctoral researchers, secure grants and advise institutions on responsible AI.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Lead AI-policy and ethics centres, shape research agendas and bridge technical AI development with social, legal and institutional needs.

blocks.text: Ph.D. routes

The long-term academic target is to become a recognised authority who can evaluate AI systems from technical, social, ethical and institutional perspectives. Lead interdisciplinary teams rather than treating ethics as an add-on to engineering. Build research programs around measurable questions such as safety, fairness, accountability, human oversight, privacy, labour effects and governance of increasingly capable AI systems.
